Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase! The Indian players are spreading out in the field and taking their respective fielding positions. Also, the two openers of the Sri Lanka Women come out, Hasini Perera and Vishmi Gunarathne. Amanjot Kaur will start the proceedings for India Women. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

Now, with a mammoth total on the board, India Women have one hand on the trophy. They carry not just the scoreboard advantage, but also the momentum and psychological edge into the second half. Sneh Rana, the series' top wicket-taker, along with a disciplined bowling unit, will look to shut the door on Sri Lanka early. As for the Lankan batters, they’ll have to overcome not only the weight of the target but also the searing heat, scoreboard pressure, and a fierce Indian attack. The odds are heavily stacked, but cricket finals have a way of springing surprises. Can Sri Lanka pull off the miraculous? Or will India seal it with dominance? All eyes on the chase, so don't go anywhere as the action for the second inning is in moments away!

For Sri Lanka Women, it was a mixed bag with the ball. Dewmi Vihanga, Malki Madara, and Sugandika Kumari picked up two wickets each, but Dewmi had to be stretchered off later and remains doubtful for the second innings, a blow that could hurt their chase if she needs to come out to bat. Inoka Ranaweera grabbed one wicket, but overall, the Lankan bowlers wilted under pressure. They bowled too many short deliveries and leaked 18 extras, a stat that reflects the strain and sloppiness under relentless Indian pressure.

Captain Harmanpreet Kaur then joined Harleen, and although they tried to rebuild, Harleen missed out on a deserving fifty, dismissed for 47. Then came Jemimah Rodrigues, who instantly injected momentum with a flurry of boundaries, playing a breezy cameo that tilted the game further in India’s favour. She and Harman added a crucial 48 runs that countered Sri Lanka’s attempts to pull things back. In the final phase, Deepti Sharma and Amanjot Kaur chipped in with priceless runs, their 37-run stand helping India breach the 340-run barrier, a score that looks near-impossible under these physically draining conditions.

The openers set the tone with a measured yet fluent start, adding 70 runs for the first wicket. Pratika Rawal departed, trying to break free, but Smriti Mandhana held the fort, anchoring and accelerating with style. She found able company in Harleen Deol, who overcame a slow start to look rock-solid at the crease. The duo’s 120-run partnership formed the spine of India’s innings, and Piumi Badalge dropping a catch of Smriti earlier just after the Powerplay cost Sri Lanka Women a lot as Mandhana reached her 11th ODI century in a blaze, smashing three consecutive boundaries to get there. Battling cramps and dehydration in the brutal heat, Smriti’s knock will go down as one of her most gutsy and glorious performances on the big stage. She eventually fell while trying to up the tempo, but her job was already done.

India Women have stamped their authority on this Tri-Nation Final, putting up a towering total of 342/7 after opting to bat first. Under sweltering, humid conditions where the heat itself felt like an opponent, the Indian batters braved it all and delivered a formidable performance, making this total look like a mountain to climb for Sri Lanka. While the Lankan bowlers did manage to pick a few wickets towards the end, in the last ten overs or so, and slowed down the scoring rate slightly, the early dominance and middle-over aggression from India ensured they soared well past the 340 mark.
